text:
Testing Methodology for Business Logic Vulnerabilities:
1. Workflow & State Mapping: Deconstruct target functionality into a formal state graph ($S_0 \to S_1 \to ... \to S_n$) identifying all implicit assumptions.
2. State Desynchronization / Skip Testing: Transmit terminal-step requests (e.g., checkout, confirmation) without executing prerequisite steps (e.g., payment submission, MFA validation).
3. Boundary & Non-Sensical Input Injection: Provide negative numeric quantities, zero-value balances, unexpected data types, or duplicate concurrent payloads to identify inadequate domain verification.
4. Client-Server Inconsistency Analysis: Intercept client-to-server payloads using a proxy to alter read-only or hidden parameters (e.g., price, discount_code, user_role, status_flag).

metadata.title: Logic Flaw Discovery and Workflow Auditing Methodology

text:
Testing methodology for unconventional input handling in business workflows:
1. Submit numeric extremes: negative values, zero, numbers exceeding integer limits (overflow/underflow), and high decimals.
2. Submit structural extremes: abnormally long strings, unicode characters, and null bytes into text fields.
3. Evaluate system responses against key boundary indicators: Does the application enforce hard constraints? Does it fail closed or open when limits are reached? Does it alter, truncate, or normalize the input unexpectedly?

metadata.title: Auditing and Fuzzing for Unconventional Input in Logic Controls

text:
Methodology for identifying excessive trust in transactional parameters:
1. Proxy passive observation: Map request parameters sent during state progression (e.g. POST /cart, POST /checkout) to check for monetary or role values.
2. In-flight parameter mutation: e.g. Intercept POST /cart, decrement numeric values to negative, zero, or small integers, and resubmit.
3. State diffing: Inspect subsequent cart retrieval (e.g. GET /cart) to verify whether the server persisted the injected value or reset it to the authoritative catalog value.

metadata.title: Transactional Parameter Tampering and Price Logic Auditing

text:
Testing methodology for unsigned numeric validation in e-commerce state machines:
1. Baseline Request Mapping: Identify all endpoints modifying order state or quantities (e.g., POST /cart, PUT /cart/items, POST /order/add).
2. Sign Inversion Injection: Intercept quantity parameters and submit negative integers (-1, -100, -999999).
3. Offset Calculation: Calculate the negative quantity required to cancel out high-value items present in the cart state without causing arithmetic underflow errors.
4. Differential State Analysis: Compare cart responses before and after negative submission to inspect line-item subtotals, overall cart balance, and checkout eligibility.

metadata.title: Numeric Sign Inversion Fuzzing on State Mutations

text: Methodology for auditing multi-channel identity update inconsistencies: 1) Identify endpoints assigning implicit trust or role elevation based on user profile fields (e.g., domain, department, organization code). 2) Map all entry points capable of mutating the trust-determining attribute (e.g., onboarding, profile settings, SSO sync, API PATCH endpoints). 3) Compare validation strictness across distinct mutation channels: check whether secondary profile update workflows bypass origin validation, format restrictions, or verification challenges enforced during initial registration. 4) Verify state persistence: confirm whether updated unverified attributes grant immediate access to protected routes.

metadata.title: Auditing Disparate Workflows for Inconsistent Security Controls

text: Methodology for auditing discount code and promotional application logic: 1) Identification: Harvest available promotional tokens, voucher strings, and gift card inputs. 2) Single-token boundary test: Replay the identical coupon token consecutively to assess immediate deduplication logic. 3) Multi-token permutation test: Interleave submissions of two or more distinct valid coupons (Token A -> Token B -> Token A) to determine if state tracking is naive/ephemeral. 4) Order lifecycle test: Verify whether applied discounts persist or reset if items are removed, modified, or re-added before final checkout submission.

metadata.title: Auditing Promotional Discount State Tracking and Replay Flaws

text: Auditing methodology for financial accumulation and primitive data type boundaries: 1) Input saturation test: Determine per-request validation limits on quantity and amount fields. 2) Boundary fuzzing via repetition: If single-payload input is bounded to small integers, automate high-volume sequential additions using single concurrency to evaluate aggregation logic. 3) Monitor state transitions for sign change: Inspect responses for sign flips indicative of 16-bit (32,767), 32-bit (2,147,483,647), or unsigned integer wrapping. 4) Wraparound alignment test: Calculate wrap offset ($Target = INT\_MAX + 1 - Wraparound$) to verify whether order placement logic evaluates wrapped negative or small values without sanity bounds.

metadata.title: Auditing Cumulative Fields for Primitive Integer Wraparound

text: Methodology for auditing multi-layer input length discrepancies and silent truncation: 1) Capacity probing: Submit unique identifiable strings of increasing lengths (e.g., 64, 128, 255, 256, 512, 1024 characters) into registration and profile fields. 2) Reflection diffing: Inspect the persisted profile view (GET /profile, API responses, or raw DB reflection) to detect silent truncation points. 3) Semantic boundary positioning: If truncation is identified at length N, craft composite strings where malicious or privileged suffixes align precisely at boundary index N, while operational routing elements (like controlled DNS subdomains) sit beyond index N. 4) Multi-channel verification: Confirm whether pre-persistence services (e.g., SMTP dispatch) operate on the untruncated string while post-persistence authorization components operate on the truncated string.

metadata.title: Auditing for Silent Truncation Discrepancies in Identity Workflows

text: Auditing methodology for dual-use endpoints and parameter-inferred privilege: 1) Identification: Catalog multi-parameter state-modifying requests (e.g., password change, profile updates, subscription adjustments). 2) Systematic parameter pruning: Iteratively drop each parameter individually (both key and value) while preserving other fields. 3) Branch behavior analysis: Observe whether missing parameters bypass checks, trigger default unauthenticated code branches, or bypass confirmation gates. 4) Identity substitution: When parameter omission bypasses validation, inject external/privileged identity handles into user-binding fields (e.g., username, uid, account_id) to verify if tenant/user isolation holds.

metadata.title: Systematic Parameter Omission and Identity Decoupling Auditing

text: Methodology for auditing multi-stage state machines and workflow validation: 1) Baseline transaction tracing: Execute a complete intended workflow ($S_0 \to S_1 \to ... \to S_n$) and record the URI, method, headers, and parameters for each transition step. 2) Transition skipping: Initialize a fresh workflow state, populate data elements, and directly transmit terminal step requests ($S_n$) without executing preceding processing requests ($S_{n-1}$, $S_{n-2}$). 3) Out-of-order execution: Test reordering steps (e.g., $S_0 \to S_2 \to S_1$) or replaying prior completion tokens in uninitialized sessions. 4) Verification: Inspect backend response status and state reflections to determine if processing advanced despite missing prerequisite states.

metadata.title: State Sequence Perturbation and Workflow Step-Skipping Auditing

text: Methodology for auditing multi-stage state machines via flow interruption: 1) Sequence tracing: Trace sequential interactions during multi-phase authentication, onboarding, or approval workflows. 2) Intermediary request dropping: Selectively drop each intermediate request (e.g., dropping step 2 of a 4-step sequence) using proxy interception rather than allowing it to reach the client or backend. 3) Out-of-order target navigation: Following the drop, initiate direct requests to subsequent steps ($S_3, S_4$) and root application views to inspect the state machine's fallback behavior. 4) State invariant auditing: Determine if the uncompleted flow defaults insecurely to elevated permissions, bypasses initialization routines, or leaks access to unfinalized profiles.

metadata.title: Auditing Multi-Stage Workflows via Flow Interruption and Request Dropping

text: Methodology for auditing circular economic loops and cash-equivalent arbitrage: 1) Asset classification: Identify all catalog items functioning as stored value, vouchers, loyalty tokens, or redeemable credit. 2) Discount eligibility probing: Apply percentage and fixed-value promotional codes to cart sessions containing cash-equivalent items to check if discounts apply. 3) Transaction cycle testing: Execute a complete purchase-to-redemption loop to compute net balance change ($\Delta = Value_{redeemed} - Cost_{settled}$). 4) Automation feasibility test: If $\Delta > 0$, construct a session handling macro or headless script chaining the sequential endpoints to evaluate whether stateful rate limits, deduplication controls, or velocity limits restrict continuous replay.

metadata.title: Auditing for Closed-Loop Currency Arbitrage and Discount Stacking

text: Methodology for auditing shared cryptographic contexts and oracle vulnerabilities: 1) State artifact cataloging: Collect all encrypted strings (cookies, hidden form tokens, query parameters, password reset blobs) across application states. 2) Oracle mapping: Identify reflection vectors where user-supplied inputs are encrypted into headers/cookies (encryption oracle), or where cookies/tokens are decrypted and reflected in UI errors/views (decryption oracle). 3) Context cross-pollination: Swap encrypted blobs between different parameters to assess if keys and algorithms are shared across functions. 4) Block cipher characterization: Alter byte lengths and truncate trailing/leading bytes to discover block size (8 or 16 bytes) and cipher mode (ECB, CBC) from backend error responses. 5) Block alignment and forgery: Apply chosen-plaintext padding to align injected tokens with cipher blocks, trim static prefix blocks, and evaluate whether reconstructed tokens authenticate successfully.

metadata.title: Auditing for Symmetric Encryption Oracles and Cross-Context Key Reuse

text: Methodology for auditing multi-layer email parser discrepancies and differential interpretation: 1) Restriction profiling: Submit unauthorized email domains to identify regex boundaries and domain whitelists. 2) MIME Encoded-Word fuzzing: Inject RFC 2047 encapsulation schemes (=?charset?encoding?encoded-text?=) using standard charsets (utf-8, us-ascii, iso-8859-1) across both Q (Quoted-Printable) and B (Base64) formats into the local-part and domain segments. 3) Obsolete charset mutation: Probe uncommon, legacy, or multi-byte encodings (e.g., utf-7, euc-jp, shift_jis, iso-2022-jp) to discover validation filter bypasses. 4) Host delimiter injection: Inject encoded delimiter characters (&AEA- for '@', unicode nulls, space padding, or escaped quotes) to test whether downstream MTAs treat the encoded block as the true recipient address while upstream validators evaluate the static trailing string.

metadata.title: Auditing Email Normalization and Parser Discrepancies via Encoding Fuzzing

text: Testing Methodology: Misuse Case Modeling and Finite State Testing for Business Logic: 1) Workflow Deconstruction: Map the complete business process, identifying business limits, behavioral assumptions, and explicit transition rules ($S_0 \to S_1 \to ... \to S_n$). 2) Misuse Case Development: Formulate test cases violating conventional assumptions—skipping intermediate verification states, executing steps in reverse, repeating non-idempotent operations, or dropping transition tokens. 3) Parameter and State Tampering: Utilize intercepting proxies (e.g., OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite) to inspect and manipulate parameters in transit, testing whether modifying read-only values or altering sequential order alters the application logic flow. 4) Asynchronous and Resource Boundary Auditing: Evaluate concurrency, timeout limits on reserved resources, and ledger updates during cancellation or unexpected workflow interruptions.

metadata.title: Finite State Machine and Misuse Case Testing Methodology

text: Methodology for Auditing Business Logic Data Validation (WSTG-BUSL-01): 1) Handoff Surface Mapping: Enumerate all data entry points and trace parameter propagation across multi-tiered workflows, back-office connectors, third-party logistics APIs, and payment aggregators. 2) Interception & Semantic Mutation: Use intercepting proxies (e.g., OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite) to inject syntactically conforming but logically invalid payloads (e.g., validly formatted SSNs belonging to deceased individuals, non-existent warehouse routing IDs, or contradictory product configurations). 3) Boundary & Routing Divergence Testing: Alter fulfillment flags, delivery method enums, or inventory status variables to determine if downstream processors accept conflicting instructions without re-checking primary database state. 4) Concurrency & Cache Window Probing: Dispatch parallel requests across multiple sessions during scheduled batch update intervals to verify whether cached validation checks permit state transitions that exceed real-time resource limits.

metadata.title: Auditing Semantic Data Validation and Multi-Tier Integration Handoffs

text: Testing Methodology for Auditing Request Forgery and Parameter Guessing (WSTG-BUSL-02): 1) Hidden Field Discovery: Enumerate hidden HTML form elements, serialized JSON attributes, and query flags across multi-stage processes. 2) Flag Inversion Testing: Identify boolean or enumerated state parameters (e.g., is_submitted=1, paid=false, role=0) and invert them during downstream operations to observe application behavior. 3) Heuristic Parameter Fuzzing: Fuzz endpoints with common debug and administrative flags (e.g., debug=1, admin=true, test=1, trace=true, verbose=1) using tools like Burp Suite or OWASP ZAP. 4) Predictable Identifier Manipulation: Inspect sequential transaction numbers or identifiers and mutate them to access or modify records belonging to other tenants or previous workflow states.

metadata.title: Methodology for Auditing Request Forgery and State Manipulation

text: Methodology for Auditing Business Logic Integrity Checks (WSTG-BUSL-03): 1) UI vs. Payload Differential Mapping: Compare rendered DOM inputs (disabled, hidden, select controls) with outgoing HTTP parameters captured in an intercepting proxy. 2) Non-Editable Parameter Fuzzing: Manually append or mutate parameters designated as fixed/read-only on the frontend to determine if server controllers accept client overrides. 3) Relational Scoping and Enumeration: Identify dropdown menus and enumerated selectors; substitute values with adjacent, non-assigned, or privileged object IDs to evaluate server-side relational authorization. 4) Referential Consistency Testing: Submit edge-case attribute pairings that violate business logic rules (e.g., impossible entity statuses, mutually exclusive options) to evaluate relational constraint checks. 5) Audit Log Resiliency Testing: Probe logging endpoints with newline injection, format string tokens, or direct file manipulation attempts to assess log immutability.

metadata.title: Auditing Relational Integrity Checks and Hidden Field Constraints

text: Methodology for Auditing Process Timing and Transactional Lifecycles (WSTG-BUSL-04): 1) Statistical Timing Side-Channel Analysis: Transmit multi-round serialized requests across valid and invalid parameter sets (e.g., username lists, coupon tokens) and compute latency confidence intervals to identify information disclosure. 2) Resource Hold and Lockout Probing: Invoke reservation endpoints (POST /reserve, POST /cart/hold) and monitor secondary concurrent sessions at incremental delays (e.g., 5 min, 15 min, 60 min) to evaluate release mechanics and DOS impact. 3) Stalled Workflow Submission: In workflows featuring dynamic pricing or expiring terms, obtain a transaction token at $T_0$, pause submission via proxy intercept or script sleep, and submit at $T_{extended}$ to verify whether the backend rejects stale state or updates pricing.

metadata.title: Auditing Timing Side-Channels and Stalled Transaction Windows

text: Methodology for Auditing Function Execution Limits (WSTG-BUSL-05): 1) Identification: Catalog all high-value endpoints enforcing operational quotas (e.g., discount coupons, free trials, document exports, voting buttons). 2) Direct Replay Testing: Intercept the execution request using Burp Suite or OWASP ZAP; replay the exact payload immediately after initial consumption to verify single-use enforcement. 3) Workflow Navigation Perturbation: Execute the target action, navigate backward in the browser session, alter unrelated cart/profile attributes, and attempt to invoke the restricted function again. 4) Concurrency Fuzzing: Dispatch concurrent parallel requests for single-use actions using Turbo Intruder to identify race conditions in quota decrement routines.

metadata.title: Auditing Function Use Limits, Replay Controls, and Quota Bounds

text: Methodology for Auditing Workflow Circumvention and Sequence Bypasses (WSTG-BUSL-06): 1) Workflow Mapping: Deconstruct multi-stage operations into discrete states, documenting side-effects triggered at each transition ($S_0 \to S_1 \to ... \to S_n$). 2) Rollback & Abort Fuzzing: Progress through transactions to points where side-effects trigger, then issue cancellations, timeouts, or cart deductions to evaluate whether rollback mechanisms are atomic and complete. 3) Order Permutation Testing: Attempt forced browsing, out-of-order execution, and repetition of non-idempotent steps using Burp Proxy or OWASP ZAP. 4) Lifecycle Differential Auditing: Compare validation mechanisms between primary creation interfaces and secondary edit/append endpoints by injecting restricted or non-compliant values into update requests.

metadata.title: Auditing Workflow Sequence Enforcement and Rollback Integrity

text: Methodology for Auditing Application-Layer Active Defenses (WSTG-BUSL-07): 1) Anomaly Test Matrix Execution: Construct a synthetic battery of misuse actions across an active session, including parameter pollution (duplicate parameters), malformed data formats (truncated JSON/XML), rapid HTTP verb switching, and unauthorized entity ID references. 2) Behavioral Velocity Probing: Dispatch business operations (e.g., voucher redemptions, profile edits, checkout reviews) at rates exceeding human capability to evaluate behavioral velocity thresholds. 3) Countermeasure Profiling: Observe server responses across the testing sequence to determine whether defenses are purely localized (e.g., single-field rejection) or systemic (e.g., session-wide tarpitting, account suspension, challenge screens). 4) Out-of-Order Workflow Injection: Intentionally violate finite state machine paths to test if invalid state jumps generate security containment events or fail open.

metadata.title: Auditing Systemic Misuse Detection and Adaptive Response Mechanisms

text: Methodology for Auditing Unexpected File Type Handling (WSTG-BUSL-08): 1) Business File Specification Review: Catalog all expected file types and operational constraints for each upload endpoint. 2) Extension & Payload Library Generation: Assemble test payloads spanning server executable scripts (.php, .jsp, .asp, .cgi), scriptable formats (.html, .svg, .xml), and unexpected binaries (.exe, .sh). 3) Multi-Vector Bypassing: Test for superficial verification tiers by: bypassing client-side JavaScript validation with an intercepting proxy; preserving dangerous extensions while modifying the Content-Type header to permitted values; mutating filename extensions (e.g., double extensions .php.jpg, null byte injections .php%00.jpg, case alterations .PhP). 4) Archive Extraction Testing: Submit ZIP/TAR archives containing nested path traversal tokens (../../shell.php) to assess extraction directory containment. 5) Execution Verification: Attempt to retrieve and invoke the uploaded files directly via the browser or API client to determine execution contexts.

metadata.title: Auditing File Upload Boundaries, MIME Validation, and Storage Execution

text: Methodology for Auditing Malicious File Ingestion and Content Defenses (WSTG-BUSL-09): 1) Functional Inventory: Map all endpoints handling file uploads, identifying allowed MIME types, intended consumers, storage locations, and downstream decompression/rendering pipelines. 2) Antivirus & Antimalware Probing: Upload harmless standard test signatures (EICAR) across permitted extension wrappers to verify if active pipeline scanning is present. 3) Extension & MIME Evasion Fuzzing: Probe upload handlers using alternative execution extensions (.phtml, .php5, .shtml, .aspx, .cshtml), case variations, trailing dots/spaces/null-bytes, and mismatched Content-Type headers. 4) Archive Path Traversal & Zip Bomb Testing: Craft ZIP files embedding path traversal sequences (..\) and high-ratio sparse files to evaluate directory extraction boundaries and resource consumption ceilings. 5) Polyglot & Macro Injection: Test file uploads containing embedded payloads (e.g., PHP code inside valid image headers, JavaScript in PDFs, CSV macro formulas) to determine if files are re-encoded and sanitized prior to storage.

metadata.title: Auditing Malicious File Ingestion, Content Filters, and Execution Boundaries
tools: Custom Zip Slip / Zip Bomb Generators

text: Methodology for Auditing Business Logic and Threat Modeling Misuse: 1) Dishonest User Threat Modeling: Identify every assumption the application makes about user intent and assess how violating that assumption benefits the user (e.g., negative quantities, step skipping, out-of-order execution, self-referrals). 2) Invariant Definition and Testing: Write explicit invariant statements for all value-handling operations (e.g., 'a user cannot approve their own request', 'a balance cannot drop below zero') and construct unit/integration tests designed to intentionally violate them. 3) Multiplexed Concurrency Testing: Use HTTP/2 single-packet multiplexing or multi-threaded runners to dispatch simultaneous requests against critical check-then-act endpoints (balance debits, voucher redemptions, inventory locks). 4) Workflow Perturbation: Intercept and replay requests out of sequence, alter hidden/derived fields, and probe endpoints using altered contextual attributes.

metadata.title: Auditing Business Logic via Adversarial Invariants and Concurrency Testing
metadata.source: OWASP Business Logic Security Cheat Sheet

text: Methodology for Taxonomic Profiling and Root-Cause Auditing of Business Logic Flaws: 1) Grouping Decomposition: Ingest suspected business logic anomalies and categorize them against CWE-840 member children rather than treating them as generic implementation bugs. 2) Dimension Classification: Evaluate whether the observed flaw is workflow-oriented (CWE-841, order of operations and state traversal), identity/ownership-oriented (CWE-283, CWE-639, CWE-708), uniqueness-oriented (CWE-837, anti-replay and single-use invariants), or resource-oriented (CWE-770, rate limiting and quotas). 3) Invariant Formulation: Convert the natural-language business rule into a formal verification assertion to facilitate differential testing and model checking. 4) Verification Oracle Selection: Select the corresponding evidence pattern to observe invariant violations (e.g., differential response codes, sign inversions, or ledger balance divergences).

metadata.title: CWE-840 Member Weakness Decomposition and Verification Methodology

text: Methodology for Auditing Behavioral Workflow Enforcement (CWE-841): 1) Workflow Mapping: Deconstruct the intended business sequence into a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of states (S_0, S_1, ..., S_terminal). 2) Step Skipping Probing: Transmit direct requests to terminal actions (S_terminal) immediately following initialization (S_0), omitting all intermediate approval, authentication, or payment requests. 3) Sequence Permutation: Submit requests in reverse or interleaved order (e.g., S_2 before S_1) to verify whether server controllers validate antecedent execution. 4) State Interruption & Dropping: Intercept and drop intermediate transition requests (e.g., role assignment or balance validation) to test whether default states fail open into privileged roles.

metadata.title: Auditing Workflow Sequence Permutations and Step Skipping

text: Methodology for Auditing TOCTOU Race Conditions (CWE-367): 1) Critical Section Identification: Catalog endpoints executing multi-step read-modify-write behaviors (e.g., voucher consumption, wallet transfers, inventory reservation). 2) Synchronization Pipeline Setup: Configure concurrency harnesses (such as Turbo Intruder or custom HTTP/2 multiplexing scripts) to transmit bursts of identical requests arriving within the same network packet or sub-millisecond timeframe. 3) State Boundary Fuzzing: Evaluate whether concurrent requests pass pre-condition gates simultaneously, observing if the system produces negative balances, multiple voucher credits, or inventory overallocations. 4) Post-Execution Reconciliation: Audit database persistence logs to identify whether conflicting threads executed without serialization aborts or locking delays.

metadata.title: Auditing TOCTOU Windows and Concurrent Request Multiplexing

text: Methodology for Auditing Single, Unique Action Enforcement (CWE-837): 1) Single-Use Endpoint Discovery: Catalog endpoints where repetition yields unfair advantage, skew, or asset duplication (e.g., voting, rating, bonus accrual, reservation locks, refunds). 2) Client-Side Tracking Tampering: Execute the action, then clear cookies, modify HTTP request headers (User-Agent, X-Forwarded-For), or use incognito/secondary session containers to determine if client-side fingerprinting is the sole control. 3) Replay and Parameter Mutation: Resend the exact request payload via Burp Repeater or curl without modification to evaluate basic replay protections. 4) Identity Parameter Substitution: If the request includes user identifiers in the body, test whether mutating caller identifiers allows re-invoking the action on behalf of other actors or re-applying benefits to the same target resource.

metadata.title: Auditing Single-Use Business Functions and Uniqueness Controls

text: Methodology for Auditing Execution Order and Behavioral Discrepancies: 1) Order-of-Operations Deconstruction: Trace request handling pipelines to isolate where decoding, parsing, access control checks, and data mutations occur. 2) Canonicalization Differential Probing: Feed uncanonicalized inputs (e.g., overlong UTF-8, double URL-encoding, dot-slash segments) into protected endpoints to determine if access control engines evaluate raw representations while downstream business layers execute decoded values. 3) Post-Redirect Body Inspection: Intercept 301/302 responses using proxy tools and examine response bodies or observe database states to detect whether downstream controllers executed actions despite unauthenticated status. 4) Switch and Logic Fuzzing: Fuzz multi-action dispatch parameters with unlisted enums, integer boundary values, and malformed types to trigger default fall-through cases or omitted break routines.

metadata.title: Auditing Control-Flow Sequencing and Behavioral Anomalies

text: Methodology for Auditing Interaction Frequency and Anti-Automation Controls (CWE-799): 1) High-Value Feature Identification: Catalog endpoints vulnerable to automated abuse (e.g., password guessing, promotional discount applications, asset downloads, email/SMS dispatching, polling/voting). 2) Baseline Velocity Calibration: Measure normal operational timing and analyze whether front-end elements (such as disabled buttons or client JS timers) can be decoupled by capturing raw HTTP requests. 3) Scaled Rate Probing: Transmit rapid, sustained request streams using automated harnesses (e.g., Burp Intruder, Turbo Intruder, or Python asyncio scripts) across varying request intervals. 4) Evasion Differential Analysis: Test rate-limit evasion mechanisms, including header mutation (X-Forwarded-For, Client-IP), session rotation, and parameter interleaving, verifying whether throttling tracks server-side identity or superficial network attributes.

metadata.title: Auditing Endpoint Velocity, Rate Limiting, and Anti-Automation Evasion

text: Methodology for Auditing Control Flow Management and Structural Scoping: 1) Static Data & Control Flow Modeling (SAST): Analyze source and compiled binaries to trace execution paths connecting untrusted inputs (sources) to business-critical operations (sinks), identifying missing handlers, unhandled return values, or fall-through blocks. 2) Synchronization Error Injection: Hook or mock synchronization primitives to return error statuses (e.g., lock acquisition timeout, deadlock detection) and verify whether callers fail closed or execute guarded actions regardless. 3) Resource Access Inversion Testing: Monitor memory/CPU allocation on unauthorized requests (e.g., large file download endpoints accessed by unprivileged users) to ensure denial-of-access terminates prior to resource retrieval. 4) Branch and Scoping Fuzzing: Fuzz multi-stage dispatch routines with unexpected parameters to identify unconditional execution of subsequent lines due to scoping defects.

metadata.title: Auditing Control Flow Sequencing, Synchronization Returns, and Scoping

text: Methodology for Auditing Execution Order and Behavioral Sequencing (CWE-696): 1) Pipeline Deconstruction: Trace request lifecycles from ingress to storage, documenting the sequential order of decoding, validation, permission checking, and resource allocation. 2) Normalization Differential Testing: Craft path payloads embedding dot-dot-slash sequences (e.g., /allowed/../sensitive) or encoded variants to determine whether path validation evaluates raw strings rather than normalized canonical paths. 3) Resource Amplification Probing: Dispatch unauthorized requests for exceptionally large files or complex reports, measuring response latency, heap allocation, and disk I/O to verify whether asset extraction precedes permission evaluation. 4) Process Privilege Verification: Audit Unix service initialization scripts and privilege-dropping routines to verify whether setgid() precedes setuid() and checks return codes.

metadata.title: Auditing Execution Order, Validation Sequencing, and Pre-Access Checks

text: Methodology for Auditing Control Flow Scoping and Execution After Redirect (CWE-705): 1) Non-Following Redirect Analysis: Configure proxy interceptors (Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP) to suppress automatic redirect following (HTTP 301/302/303/307). Examine raw HTTP response bodies returned on unauthorized requests to identify leaked sensitive DOM elements, database metrics, or server status data. 2) Post-Redirect State Mutation Verification: Target modification endpoints (e.g., POST /admin/user/delete) without authorization; observe whether backend records update in persistent storage despite the client receiving an HTTP 302 Redirect to /login. 3) SAST Control-Flow Modeling: Trace Abstract Syntax Trees (AST) and Control Flow Graphs (CFG) using static analysis tools to verify that all branching paths calling redirect utilities contain explicit terminating return/break/exit instructions. 4) Unhandled Exception Probing: Submit malformed payloads designed to provoke unhandled runtime exceptions (e.g., unresolvable DNS hostnames, null pointers) to evaluate whether failure modes crash thread pools or yield uncaught container teardowns.

metadata.title: Auditing Control Flow Scoping, Execution After Redirect, and Exception Handling

text: Methodology for Auditing Authentication Rate Limiting and Lockout Controls (CWE-307): 1) Boundary Calibration: Transmit rapid, repeated invalid authentication requests to target endpoints (POST /login, REST token routes) to determine if lockouts, progressive delays, or CAPTCHA challenges trigger at specific failure thresholds (e.g., 3, 5, or 10 attempts). 2) Concurrency & Multiplexing Probing: Dispatch parallel authentication streams across multiple concurrent connections to test whether backend delay mechanisms (such as thread sleep) can be overwhelmed by volumetric throughput. 3) IP and Header Spoofing Evasion: Test whether rotating headers (X-Forwarded-For, Client-IP) or resetting cookies resets failed attempt counters, identifying whether state tracking is pinned to persistent server-side account identities or client-controllable indicators.

metadata.title: Auditing Authentication Velocity, Lockout Thresholds, and Bypass Resilience

text: Methodology for Navigating SDLC Weakness Taxonomies (CWE-699): 1) Functional Domain Identification: Locate the specific software engineering domain implicated by the anomalous behavior (e.g., File Handling Issues [1219], Concurrency Issues [557], Data Validation Issues [1215], or Business Logic Errors [840]). 2) Hierarchical Down-Traversal: Move from the top-level Category to member Classes and Base weaknesses to locate the exact programmatic failure mechanism. 3) Phase and Mode Correlation: Correlate the weakness against the mode of introduction across architecture, implementation, or deployment to define corresponding test oracles and defensive invariant checks.

metadata.title: Navigating CWE-699 Hierarchies for Weakness Classification

text: Methodology for Auditing Insecure Design and Architectural Trust Flaws (CWE-1348): 1) Architectural Threat Modeling: Conduct design reviews examining data flow diagrams (DFDs) and trust boundaries, identifying assumptions where client compliance or frontend GUI controls are mistaken for backend security enforcement. 2) Client State Decoupling: Intercept API interactions using proxies (Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP) to submit requests that omit intermediate steps, supply conflicting parameter pairs, or manipulate immutable fields (prices, roles, identifiers). 3) Boundary Crossing and Injection Auditing: Test parameter propagation between front-facing web tiers and backend microservices to locate trust boundary violations (e.g., HTTP request smuggling via CWE-444, parameter tampering via CWE-472). 4) Anti-Automation Stress Testing: Dispatch parallel, high-velocity transactions against value-granting workflows using Turbo Intruder to identify unthrottled architectural design omissions (CWE-799).

metadata.title: Auditing Architectural Trust Boundaries and Insecure Design Flaws

text: Testing playbook: map every endpoint that accepts an object identifier, including path segments, query parameters, JSON body keys, GraphQL node IDs, and batch arrays. Create two accounts in the same tenant and one in a different tenant. Capture identifiers from list, search, export, and notification responses, then replay each read and write with the other session using Burp Repeater or an Autorize-style extension. Fuzz sequential integers, UUID variants, and encoded IDs. For each response, diff status code, body length, and ownership fields. Tools: Burp Suite (Repeater, Intruder, Autorize), OWASP ZAP, Postman, and a custom Python requests harness. Target phases: endpoint inventory, identifier harvesting, horizontal replay, nested-resource replay, and impact confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-283 Testing Methodology: Unverified Resource Ownership

text: Testing playbook: inventory every key-bearing parameter, including path, query, JSON body, GraphQL global IDs, and batch arrays. Establish two tenants and capture identifiers from list, export, and notification responses. Replay each request with the other tenant key and compare status, length, and object fields. Run enumeration against numeric and time-ordered identifiers with ffuf or Burp Intruder. Test write methods separately because read-only checks often hide mutation impact. Tools: Burp Suite with Autorize, OWASP ZAP, ffuf, Postman, and a Python requests harness. Target phases: key inventory, key harvesting, substitution, enumeration, batch and GraphQL coverage, and write-impact confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-639 Testing Methodology: IDOR and Object Key Substitution

text: Testing playbook: map the full reset flow and capture token issuance, delivery, and consumption. Test token reuse after a successful reset, token lifetime after expiry, entropy and predictability, and whether the token is bound to the account. Manipulate Host, X-Forwarded-Host, and absolute reset URL parameters to test link poisoning. Brute-force short OTPs with Turbo Intruder using parallel requests while measuring per-account and per-IP throttling. Compare responses for valid, invalid, and unknown accounts to detect enumeration. Tools: Burp Suite, Turbo Intruder, OWASP ZAP, and a custom Python harness. Target phases: flow mapping, token analysis, replay, brute force, host poisoning, and enumeration.

metadata.title: CWE-640 Testing Methodology: Password Recovery Abuse

text: Testing playbook: review create and upload handlers for owner, tenant, group, and path fields. Fuzz those fields with victim and administrative values, then verify the persisted ownership through a follow-up read and, for files, through metadata exposed by the application. Test symlink and predictable-path behavior by uploading linked or crafted filenames. Exercise logout and resource release to see whether ownership is restored correctly. Tools: Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, Postman, and a custom filesystem harness. Target phases: handler review, field tampering, filesystem ownership, release behavior, and cross-account impact.

metadata.title: CWE-708 Testing Methodology: Ownership Assignment Tampering

text: Testing playbook: inventory endpoints that accept counts, arrays, page sizes, uploads, or create persistent resources. Send a single oversized request and measure latency, memory, and response size. Send parallel creation requests with Turbo Intruder or k6 and count resources per account. Test whether quotas reset on logout, are keyed only by IP, or can be bypassed with a second tenant. Measure the impact on a separate legitimate account. Tools: Burp Suite, Turbo Intruder, k6, and OWASP ZAP. Target phases: surface inventory, single-request amplification, rate testing, quota bypass, and availability impact.

metadata.title: CWE-770 Testing Methodology: Unbounded Resource Allocation

text: Testing playbook: map acquire and release pairs for locks, database connections, sessions, and temporary files. Interleave acquire and release with a concurrency harness and use single-packet or last-byte synchronization to widen the race window. Probe stale handles after release and check whether they return another principal's data or partially committed state. Repeat under load to confirm reproducibility. Tools: Burp Suite, Turbo Intruder, a custom asyncio or threading harness, and OWASP ZAP. Target phases: lifecycle mapping, interleaving, stale-handle probing, load reproducibility, and impact confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-826 Testing Methodology: Premature Resource Release

text: Testing playbook: select single-use or balance-bearing operations and capture one valid request. Duplicate it 10 to 50 times and send with last-byte synchronization, an HTTP/2 single-packet attack, or a custom asyncio harness. Compare the number of success responses, ledger entries, and final balance against a single execution. Tune the window by adding jitter and by targeting the check and write phases. Tools: Burp Suite, Turbo Intruder, k6, and a custom asyncio harness. Target phases: target selection, request capture, concurrency tuning, invariant measurement, and reproducibility.

metadata.title: CWE-362 Testing Methodology: Race Condition and Concurrent State Mutation

text: Testing playbook: proxy all client-server traffic and identify fields computed in JavaScript, including price, total, discount, role, quantity, and file type. Modify each field and replay the request, then confirm the persisted value with a follow-up read. Disable JavaScript or call the endpoint directly to test whether UI gates are the only control. Tools: Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, browser devtools, and Postman. Target phases: traffic capture, field identification, tamper replay, direct endpoint access, and persistence confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-602 Testing Methodology: Client-Side Control Bypass

text: Testing playbook: enumerate cookies, headers, and parameters that influence access decisions. Mutate role, admin, tenant, and user_id values and replay the request. Test JWT signature enforcement, algorithm confusion, and claim tampering with jwt_tool. Test X-Forwarded-For, X-Original-URL, and similar headers against IP-based or path-based controls. Confirm elevated access on a protected endpoint. Tools: Burp Suite, jwt_tool, OWASP ZAP, and Postman. Target phases: input inventory, mutation, JWT analysis, proxy-header testing, and impact confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-807 Testing Methodology: Untrusted Input in Security Decisions

text: Testing playbook: capture every form and enumerate hidden, readonly, and cookie-based fields. Mutate price, discount, user_id, role, and status values, then replay the request and compare the persisted state with an independent server-side calculation. Test subsequent workflow steps to see whether the tampered value is re-derived or carried forward. Tools: Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, browser devtools, and Postman. Target phases: form inventory, hidden-field mutation, persistence check, workflow replay, and impact confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-472 Testing Methodology: Assumed-Immutable Parameter Tampering

text: Testing playbook: map endpoints that bind request bodies to models. Discover the model fields from responses, error messages, and framework conventions, then inject privileged keys such as role, is_admin, balance, verified, and tenant_id. Test nested objects and alternate content types. Verify persistence in a fresh session and by exercising the privileged capability. Tools: Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, Postman, and a custom JSON fuzzer. Target phases: endpoint inventory, field discovery, injection, persistence, and privilege confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-915 Testing Methodology: Mass Assignment

text: Testing playbook: review comparison sites for passwords, tokens, roles, and signatures. Fuzz types and encodings with 0e hashes, true/1, null, arrays, case variants, and Unicode normalization forms. Test prefix and substring acceptance on tokens. Measure response timing for secret comparisons to detect non-constant-time behavior. Tools: Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, hashcat for magic-hash generation, and a custom Python fuzzer. Target phases: comparison inventory, type fuzzing, encoding variants, prefix testing, and timing analysis.

metadata.title: CWE-697 Testing Methodology: Comparison Logic Bypass

text: Testing playbook: capture the pre-authentication session identifier and note how it is transported (cookie, URL, hidden field). Deliver the identifier to a second browser through a URL, cookie, or sibling subdomain, then authenticate as the victim. Compare the pre- and post-login identifiers and attempt to reuse the pre-auth identifier from the attacker session. Test logout, password change, and privilege elevation for rotation. Tools: Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, browser devtools, and a Python requests harness. Target phases: lifecycle mapping, pre-auth capture, fixation delivery, post-login comparison, and hijack confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-384 Testing Methodology: Session Identifier Fixation

text: Testing playbook: capture the password-change request and identify the current-password or re-authentication field. Remove, blank, or replay it, then verify whether the server still updates the credential. Test CSRF by replaying the request from a cross-origin page without a token. Log in with the new password and confirm the old one fails, then check whether other sessions remain valid. Tools: Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, Postman, and browser devtools. Target phases: flow mapping, current-password removal, CSRF testing, credential verification, and session invalidation.

metadata.title: CWE-620 Testing Methodology: Password Change Without Re-authentication

text: Testing playbook: inventory endpoints that perform expensive queries, recursive parsing, report generation, or large allocations. Measure the amplification ratio between request bytes and server CPU, memory, or latency. Send nested JSON, deeply recursive structures, and large pagination values within accepted content limits. Use slowhttptest or a custom harness to hold connections open and exhaust the pool. Tools: Burp Suite, k6, slowhttptest, and OWASP ZAP. Target phases: endpoint inventory, amplification measurement, nested payload testing, connection exhaustion, and fail-open impact.

metadata.title: CWE-400 Testing Methodology: Resource Exhaustion Amplification

text: Testing playbook: inventory lock acquisition and release paths for shared resources. Trigger double unlock and unlock-without-lock with invalid inputs. Interleave two operations that acquire locks in opposite order and observe deadlock. Test predictable lock files and names by pre-creating them. Use a custom threading harness or Turbo Intruder for concurrency. Tools: custom threading harness, Burp Suite, Turbo Intruder, and stress-ng. Target phases: lock inventory, pairing tests, order interleaving, predictable names, and deadlock impact.

metadata.title: CWE-667 Testing Methodology: Locking Discipline Failure

text: Testing playbook: enumerate the factors that define each security decision and identify which ones the comparison checks. Test alternative schemes, path suffixes, encoded separators, case variants, and Unicode normalization. For multi-tenant systems, vary tenant_id independently of object_id. Tools: Burp Suite, ffuf, OWASP ZAP, and custom wordlists. Target phases: factor enumeration, gap analysis, scheme and path testing, tenant and type testing, and impact confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-1023 Testing Methodology: Missing-Factor Comparison Bypass

text: Testing playbook: inventory every parameter that resolves to a file, template, log, backup, or export path, including headers such as Content-Disposition filenames. Fuzz with ../, ....//, ..%2f, %252e%252e%252f, backslash, absolute paths, drive letters, UNC paths, and null bytes. Determine whether validation happens before or after decoding by comparing encoded variants that decode to the same path. Confirm reads of a known file outside the root and test write endpoints for overwrite impact. Tools: Burp Suite, ffuf, dotdotpwn, and OWASP ZAP. Target phases: parameter inventory, encoding fuzzing, canonicalization gap analysis, impact testing, and privilege review.

metadata.title: CWE-22 Testing Methodology: Path Traversal

text: Testing playbook: inventory features that invoke external programs, including diagnostics, conversions, archives, backups, and PDF or image processing. Inject semicolon, pipe, ampersand, backtick, $(), and newline payloads, then repeat with URL and double-URL encoding. Test argument injection against wrappers that accept switches such as find, tar, rsync, and ImageMagick. Confirm execution with a time delay and an out-of-band DNS or HTTP callback rather than relying on command output. Tools: Burp Suite, Commix, OWASP ZAP, and Burp Collaborator. Target phases: feature inventory, metacharacter injection, encoding variants, argument injection, and out-of-band proof.

metadata.title: CWE-78 Testing Methodology: OS Command Injection

text: Testing playbook: inventory parameters used in WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, HAVING, and identifier positions such as sort and table. Probe with single and double quotes, comment markers, and arithmetic to detect syntax influence. Use boolean and time-based blind payloads where output is suppressed, and attempt UNION extraction with matching column counts. Test stacked queries where the driver permits them, and check for authentication bypass with tautologies. Tools: sqlmap, Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, and a custom Python fuzzer. Target phases: parameter inventory, syntax probing, blind testing, UNION and stacked queries, and privilege review.

metadata.title: CWE-89 Testing Methodology: SQL Injection

text: Testing playbook: map every reflection point and stored field that is later rendered, including admin, support, and email views. Classify the output context for each sink and craft payloads that break that specific context: tag injection in the body, attribute breakout, javascript: URLs, and script-context string escapes. Trace DOM sources such as location, referrer, and postMessage to sinks such as innerHTML, document.write, and eval. Confirm execution with a benign alert or an out-of-band callback, and review Content-Security-Policy and cookie flags. Tools: Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, browser devtools, and XSStrike. Target phases: mapping, context classification, payload testing, DOM tracing, and execution confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-79 Testing Methodology: Cross-Site Scripting

text: Testing playbook: discover serialized formats in cookies, hidden fields, uploads, APIs, and message queues by looking for magic bytes such as rO0AB for Java, aced0005 for .NET, and O: for PHP. Decode and inspect the structure without triggering execution where possible. Generate benign gadget chains with ysoserial or language equivalents and deliver them while watching for out-of-band callbacks or side effects. Test YAML, XML, and format loaders for unsafe constructors. Tools: ysoserial, Burp Suite, Java Deserialization Scanner, and a custom Python harness. Target phases: discovery, format recognition, chain generation, side-effect testing, and loader hardening.

metadata.title: CWE-502 Testing Methodology: Insecure Deserialization

text: Testing playbook: inventory every endpoint that creates, updates, deletes, or transfers, and record its method and encoding. Check whether a token parameter exists and whether removing, blanking, or reusing another user's token is rejected. Build a cross-origin proof of concept that auto-submits the request and observe whether the victim's state changes. Test SameSite behavior, Origin and Referer validation, and whether GET variants mutate state. Tools: Burp Suite with the CSRF PoC generator, OWASP ZAP, and browser devtools. Target phases: endpoint inventory, token testing, cross-origin PoC, SameSite and Origin analysis, and impact confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-352 Testing Methodology: CSRF

text: Testing playbook: inventory every upload endpoint, including avatars, attachments, imports, and document previews, and determine where files land and how they are served. Test extension filters with executable extensions, double extensions, trailing dots and spaces, case variants, and null bytes. Spoof Content-Type and magic bytes to satisfy image checks, then attempt polyglot files. Request the stored file directly and verify whether the server executes it or renders active content. Tools: Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, ExifTool, and a custom polyglot generator. Target phases: surface inventory, extension and MIME bypass, content sniffing bypass, storage testing, and serving review.

metadata.title: CWE-434 Testing Methodology: Unrestricted File Upload

text: Testing playbook: inventory endpoints that accept XML directly or indirectly through SOAP, SAML, SVG, DOCX, or RSS imports. Inject a DOCTYPE with an external entity referencing a local file and reflect the entity in a response field. Where output is suppressed, use parameter entities and an attacker-hosted DTD to exfiltrate over HTTP, or a DNS callback to confirm resolution. Test entity expansion limits with nested entities. Tools: Burp Suite, XXEinjector, OWASP ZAP, and Burp Collaborator. Target phases: surface inventory, entity injection, out-of-band exfiltration, parser hardening review, and impact confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-611 Testing Methodology: XML External Entity Injection

text: Testing playbook: inventory features that fetch URLs, including previews, webhooks, imports, PDF renderers, and image proxies. Substitute localhost, loopback, private ranges, and the cloud metadata endpoint, and try alternate encodings such as decimal, octal, IPv6, and bracketed forms. Test redirect chains where the first hop is allowed and the second is internal, and DNS rebinding where validation and fetch resolve differently. Use timing, error text, and response length as side channels. Tools: Burp Suite, SSRFmap, Interactsh, and OWASP ZAP. Target phases: surface inventory, internal probing, metadata testing, bypass testing, and impact confirmation.

metadata.title: CWE-918 Testing Methodology: SSRF

text: Testing playbook: inventory fields and parsers validated by regex, including headers such as User-Agent and Referer. Analyze patterns for nested quantifiers and overlapping alternations, then generate inputs with long runs of a character adjacent to a failing suffix. Measure response time as input length grows and confirm superlinear or exponential scaling. Repeat across worker processes and confirm impact on a second user. Tools: Burp Suite, dedicated ReDoS tooling, a custom Python harness, and k6. Target phases: surface inventory, complexity analysis, adversarial generation, scaling measurement, and availability impact.

metadata.title: CWE-1333 Testing Methodology: ReDoS

text: Testing playbook: enumerate every authentication, registration, reset, and token endpoint and record its scheme. Trace form actions, redirects, and iframe or script sources for HTTP origins. Disable automatic HTTPS upgrades or use a proxy to observe whether the client ever issues a cleartext request. Capture traffic with Wireshark or a transparent proxy and search for POST bodies containing password parameters. Confirm HSTS and Secure cookie flags with testssl.sh or an equivalent scanner. The target phases are scheme inventory, action tracing, mixed-content review, and capture verification.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-01: Transport Security Verification for Authentication Flows
target_phases: Mixed content and script origin review

text: Testing playbook: inventory administrative consoles, databases, brokers, and integration endpoints, including non-standard ports and paths. Collect vendor default pairs from documentation and public datasets, then attempt them within the authorized scope and rate limits. On success, record the account's capabilities without changing production state, and check whether a forced password change was bypassable. Test demo and service accounts separately. The target phases are interface inventory, default lookup, controlled attempts, and capability review.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-02: Default Credential Discovery and Verification

text: Testing playbook: establish baseline responses for valid and invalid credentials, then send increasing failure counts for one account and record when delay, CAPTCHA, or lock appears. Repeat with rotated source IPs, sessions, and headers to test aggregation. Simulate a small distributed credential-stuffing run within scope and measure the success-to-attempt ratio. Verify that lockout recovery is time-based and notified, and that it cannot be triggered indefinitely against a victim. The target phases are baseline, threshold measurement, bypass testing, distributed simulation, and recovery review.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-03: Lockout Threshold and Bypass Testing

text: Testing playbook: build a route inventory from framework definitions, JavaScript bundles, and crawling, then request each route without a session and record status and body. Repeat with method overrides, path case changes, trailing slashes, encoded segments, and alternate hosts or ports. Test client-supplied flags, cookies, and headers such as X-Original-URL or X-Rewrite-URL. Confirm bypass by exercising a protected action, not just by viewing a page. The target phases are route inventory, direct access, variation testing, flag manipulation, and host review.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-04: Authentication Bypass Surface Testing
target_phases: Route inventory from framework and crawling

text: Testing playbook: enable remember-me, capture the persistent cookie, and decode it to determine whether it contains a password, username, or opaque token. Measure entropy and test whether changing the username reproduces a valid token. Replay the cookie from a second browser, then log out and retry, then change the password and retry. Observe whether the validator rotates on each use. The target phases are inventory, decoding, replay, revocation, and predictability.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-05: Persistent Token Analysis and Replay Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory responses that contain personal data, tokens, or one-time codes, and inspect their cache headers. Log in, view the pages, log out, then use the back button and browser history to test recovery. Inspect disk cache and the back-forward cache with devtools. Test a shared proxy path by checking whether a personalized response is served to a second session, and review autocomplete attributes on sensitive fields. The target phases are response inventory, header inspection, back recovery, proxy testing, and autocomplete review.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-06: Cache Header and Post-Logout Recovery Testing

text: Testing playbook: discover the documented policy and test the boundaries with one-character-short values, long passphrases, Unicode, and whitespace. Submit common and breached passwords to confirm the blocklist. Bypass the client by posting directly to the registration and reset endpoints, and confirm the server enforces the same rules. Compare create, change, and reset paths for parity. The target phases are policy discovery, boundary testing, blocklist testing, client bypass, and reset parity.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-07: Password Policy Boundary Testing

text: Testing playbook: map the recovery flow and record every question and validation rule. Assess each question for public discoverability and answer-space size, and test case, whitespace, and punctuation normalization. Measure rate limits and lockout on wrong answers, including distributed attempts. Confirm takeover by completing the reset and authenticating as the victim in a controlled test account. The target phases are flow mapping, question review, answer-space estimation, rate-limit testing, and takeover confirmation.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-08: Knowledge-Based Recovery Testing

text: Testing playbook: map both flows and capture token issuance and consumption. Test token entropy, expiry, replay after success, and binding to the account. Manipulate Host, X-Forwarded-Host, and reset URL parameters to test link poisoning. Attempt a password change without the current password and verify whether other sessions survive. The target phases are flow mapping, token analysis, replay, poisoning, and session invalidation.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-09: Change and Reset Flow Abuse Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory every channel that authenticates the account, including mobile apps, public APIs, IVR, support tooling, and legacy endpoints. Compare required factors, lockout, and session protections against the primary flow. Attempt to authenticate through the weakest channel with credentials that the primary flow would reject without MFA. Review support-initiated resets and whether cross-channel anomalies are correlated. The target phases are channel inventory, factor comparison, weak-channel exploitation, support review, and correlation checks.

metadata.title: WSTG-ATHN-10: Cross-Channel Authentication Parity Testing

text: Testing playbook: collect a large sample of identifiers and run entropy and pattern analysis with Burp Sequencer. Inspect cookies and tokens for encoded user data or timestamps. Test idle and absolute expiry, and whether the identifier rotates at login. Attempt to forge or modify client-side state and observe whether the server accepts it. The target phases are sampling, entropy analysis, state inspection, expiry testing, and forgery attempts.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-01: Session Schema Collection and Entropy Testing

text: Testing playbook: capture every Set-Cookie header and inventory name, flags, domain, path, and expiry. Verify Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite values, and test whether document.cookie can read sensitive cookies. Check whether the cookie is sent to sibling subdomains or over HTTP, and whether expiry exceeds the session policy. The target phases are inventory, flag inspection, scope review, and access testing.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-02: Cookie Attribute Audit

text: Testing playbook: capture the pre-authentication identifier and determine its transport. Deliver it to a second browser through a URL, a sibling-subdomain cookie, or a session-adoption parameter, then authenticate as the victim. Compare pre- and post-login identifiers and attempt reuse from the attacker browser. Test logout and privilege change for rotation. The target phases are capture, delivery, comparison, reuse, and adoption review.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-03: Fixation Delivery and Rotation Testing

text: Testing playbook: identify every location where session or reset tokens appear by inspecting URLs, forms, headers, and client storage. Load pages with third-party resources and inspect the Referer header. Review proxy and application logs for token values. Test hidden fields for tampering and replay. The target phases are location inventory, URL and referrer inspection, log review, and hidden-field testing.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-04: Token Exposure Channel Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory mutating endpoints and their encodings. Test token absence, blank values, static tokens, and cross-user token reuse. Build a cross-origin proof of concept and confirm the victim's state changes. Test SameSite behavior and Origin or Referer validation, including GET variants. The target phases are endpoint inventory, token testing, cross-origin PoC, SameSite and Origin checks, and impact confirmation.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-05: CSRF Token and Origin Validation Testing

text: Testing playbook: capture the session and any derived tokens, log out, then replay each credential against protected endpoints. Test remember-me and API tokens separately. Use the back button and history to check cached page recovery. Verify that logout is a POST with CSRF protection. The target phases are flow mapping, replay, token revocation, cache checks, and CSRF testing.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-06: Logout Termination Testing

text: Testing playbook: determine the documented idle and absolute timeouts. Capture a session and replay it after increasing idle intervals to find the real threshold. Keep a session active with periodic requests to test the absolute cap. Disable or alter client timers to confirm server enforcement. Review step-up requirements for sensitive actions. The target phases are policy discovery, idle measurement, absolute measurement, client bypass, and step-up review.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-07: Session Expiry Measurement

text: Testing playbook: enumerate session keys written by each flow and identify shared or generically named keys. Prime a key in one flow, complete it, then exercise another module to see whether the value is consumed. Test whether pre-authentication values survive login. Review whether authorization reads session flags or server records. The target phases are key inventory, priming, collision testing, persistence checks, and source review.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-08: Session Variable Priming Tests

text: Testing playbook: enumerate token acquisition vectors including XSS, cleartext, and shared storage. Import the token into a separate browser and network context and replay it. Open concurrent sessions from distant locations and observe detection. Review device binding, rotation, and revocation controls, and test one-click revoke-all. The target phases are acquisition, replay, detection, binding review, and revocation.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-09: Hijack and Replay Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory TLS endpoints, including non-standard ports and internal services. Enumerate supported protocols and cipher suites with testssl.sh or sslyze, and check certificate chain, key size, hostname, and expiry. Test whether the client rejects an invalid certificate, and review HSTS and renegotiation settings. The target phases are inventory, protocol enumeration, certificate validation, client testing, and configuration review.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-01: TLS Configuration Scanning

text: Testing playbook: locate attacker-visible ciphertext such as cookies, tokens, and hidden fields. Flip bytes in preceding blocks and compare error messages, status codes, and response bodies for padding versus content failures. Measure timing with many samples where responses are uniform. Use PadBuster or a custom harness to confirm byte-wise recovery, then attempt forgery. The target phases are inventory, error differentials, timing, decryption validation, and forgery.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-02: Padding Oracle Probing

text: Testing playbook: inventory all channels that carry sensitive data, including web, API, email, database, cache, and telemetry. Capture traffic and classify payloads for credentials, tokens, and personal data. Scan for cleartext service ports and review third-party integrations for TLS. The target phases are inventory, capture, classification, port review, and integration checks.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-03: Channel and Payload Inspection

text: Testing playbook: inventory every cryptographic operation and identify algorithms, modes, IV handling, and key sources. Analyze captured hashes and ciphertext with CyberChef for structure and ECB patterns, then validate crackability with hashcat on a controlled sample. Review client binaries and configuration for hard-coded keys. The target phases are inventory, analysis, key review, cracking validation, and migration assessment.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-04: Cryptographic Construction Review

text: Testing playbook: send unique markers in every parameter and search responses for reflections. Classify each reflection context and craft a payload that breaks it. Confirm execution in a real browser with a benign callback, and trace DOM sources to sinks. Review CSP and cookie flags. The target phases are inventory, context classification, payload construction, execution confirmation, and CSP review.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-01: Reflection Point and Context Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory every field that persists and is later displayed, including names, comments, tickets, and filenames. Inject benign markers and payloads, then view the content in every consumer, including admin and email views. Attempt sanitizer bypasses with mutation XSS and encoded attributes. Confirm execution in a browser. The target phases are inventory, injection, cross-view checks, bypass testing, and execution confirmation.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-02: Stored Payload Lifecycle Testing

text: Testing playbook: build a route and method matrix from documentation, framework routes, and crawling. Send each route with GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS, both authenticated and unauthenticated. Test X-HTTP-Method-Override and similar headers. Confirm bypass by performing a protected action. The target phases are inventory, verb substitution, override testing, HEAD and OPTIONS behavior, and authorization parity.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-03: Method Matrix Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory parameters that influence security or money. Send duplicates in different orders and encodings, and compare what the WAF blocks versus what the backend honors. Test array notation and scalar coercion. Confirm impact on a security decision or price. The target phases are inventory, duplicate injection, tier comparison, encoded variants, and impact confirmation.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-04: Parameter Pollution Probing

text: Testing playbook: inventory parameters in WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, and identifiers. Probe with quotes and comments, then boolean and time-based payloads. Attempt UNION extraction and stacked queries where supported. Review database privileges and error handling. The target phases are inventory, syntax probing, blind testing, UNION testing, and privilege review.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-05: SQL Injection Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory login, search, and profile lookups backed by LDAP. Inject *, (, ), |, and NUL, and test filter termination with )(uid=*. Attempt wildcard authentication and directory enumeration, using blind techniques where errors are hidden. Review the bind account privileges. The target phases are inventory, metacharacter probing, bypass testing, enumeration, and privilege review.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-06: LDAP Filter Injection Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory endpoints that build or accept XML, including SOAP and import flows. Inject <, >, &, quotes, and closing tags into fields. Attempt duplicate fields and comment-based truncation. Review parser schema and entity settings. The target phases are inventory, metacharacter probing, element injection, duplicate testing, and parser review.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-07: XML Structure Injection Testing

text: Testing playbook: identify paths that process SSI by testing benign directives and observing output. Inject exec and include directives into reflected fields and uploads, then request the stored file. Review server configuration for Includes options and handler mappings. The target phases are path discovery, directive injection, upload testing, reflection testing, and configuration review.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-08: SSI Directive Injection Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory features backed by XML and XPath, especially login and search. Probe with quotes, brackets, and boolean operators, and attempt tautology bypass. Use blind substring tests where output is hidden, and review error messages for expression leakage. The target phases are inventory, probing, bypass testing, blind extraction, and error review.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-09: XPath Injection Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory contact forms, invitations, and mailbox features. Inject encoded CRLF into addresses, subjects, and mailbox names, and observe whether additional headers or recipients appear. Test IMAP commands and outbound relay behavior. The target phases are inventory, CRLF injection, header injection, IMAP commands, and relay abuse.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-10: Mail Protocol Injection Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory features that evaluate expressions or include files, such as language selectors, themes, and plugins. Test traversal, null bytes, wrappers, and remote URLs. Check whether uploaded files can be included or executed. Review interpreter configuration for allow_url_include and dangerous functions. The target phases are inventory, include testing, wrapper and traversal, upload checks, and configuration review.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-11: Code and Inclusion Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory features that call external programs. Inject semicolon, pipe, ampersand, backtick, $(), and newline, then repeat with encoding. Test argument injection against wrappers such as find and tar. Confirm execution with a time delay and an out-of-band callback. The target phases are inventory, metacharacter injection, encoding variants, argument injection, and out-of-band confirmation.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-12: Command Injection Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory native endpoints and logging paths that may use input as a format. Inject %x, %s, %p, and %n, and observe output leakage or crashes. Validate disclosure under a debugger where possible. Review logging calls for parameterization. The target phases are inventory, probing, disclosure validation, crash testing, and logging review.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-13: Format Specifier Testing

text: Testing playbook: map where submitted data is stored and every component that later reads it, including reports, exports, admin panels, and batch jobs. Inject markers and benign payloads, then trigger the downstream consumer and observe execution. Allow time for scheduled jobs. Review whether each sink revalidates and encodes. The target phases are data flow mapping, injection, consumer enumeration, delayed checks, and sink review.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-14: Second-Order Vulnerability Testing

text: Testing playbook: fingerprint parsers with timing and malformed requests, then test CRLF injection in redirects, filenames, and headers. Send CL.TE and TE.CL probes with precise timing, and confirm desynchronization by observing a subsequent request's response. Test cache poisoning where a shared cache exists. The target phases are fingerprinting, CRLF injection, conflict testing, desynchronization validation, and cache poisoning confirmation.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-15: Splitting and Smuggling Testing

text: Testing playbook: send absolute-form targets, CONNECT, TRACE, and unusual methods, and observe responses. Test proxy-style headers and whether internal hosts are reachable through the web tier. Review configuration for unintended proxy modules. The target phases are form inventory, absolute-form testing, method probing, reachability checks, and proxy review.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-16: Incoming Request Form Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory features that generate absolute URLs or route by host. Send arbitrary Host, X-Forwarded-Host, and X-Forwarded-Server values and inspect emails, redirects, and cache behavior. Test whether an unknown host reaches a different application. Verify the allowlist. The target phases are inventory, header injection, link inspection, routing and cache testing, and allowlist verification.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-17: Host Header Manipulation Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory preview, email, report, and notification features that render templates. Probe with arithmetic and string expressions across engine syntaxes, fingerprint the engine, then test context objects and sandbox escapes. Confirm impact with file read or command execution in a controlled manner. The target phases are inventory, probes, fingerprinting, sandbox testing, and impact confirmation.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-18: Template Injection Testing

text: Testing playbook: inventory URL-fetching features. Probe localhost, private ranges, and metadata endpoints, and try decimal, octal, IPv6, and bracketed encodings. Test redirects from allowed to internal hosts and DNS rebinding. Use timing and error differences as side channels. The target phases are inventory, internal probing, metadata testing, bypass testing, and impact confirmation.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-19: SSRF Testing

text: Testing playbook: proxy the entire OAuth exchange and record the authorization request, the redirect with the token, and the client's session-establishment request. Decode the token and identify which claims the client trusts. Replay the session request with a different email, subject, or username and observe whether a new session is issued. Confirm by accessing a victim-only page. Review whether the client performs any back-channel validation. The target phases are flow capture, claim decoding, rewrite replay, session confirmation, and validation review.

metadata.title: OAuth Implicit Flow Authentication Bypass: Testing Methodology

text: Testing playbook: capture the complete linking flow and inspect whether a state parameter exists, is random, and is validated against the session. Attempt to complete a link started in one browser from a second browser or session. Simulate the victim by delivering the paused final request to an authenticated browser, then log in through the attacker's social account to confirm access. The target phases are flow capture, state analysis, cross-session completion, victim simulation, and access confirmation.

metadata.title: Forced OAuth Profile Linking: Testing Methodology

text: Testing playbook: capture the authorization request and enumerate redirect_uri variants, including extra path segments, encoded traversal, alternate ports, and userinfo tricks. Look for same-origin endpoints that reflect or forward query strings, and confirm the provider follows the crafted target. Deliver the URL to the victim, capture the code from the leak endpoint, and exchange it for a session. The target phases are request capture, redirect testing, leak discovery, victim delivery, and exchange confirmation.

metadata.title: OAuth Account Hijacking via redirect_uri: Testing Methodology

text: Testing playbook: enumerate client endpoints that accept a destination and redirect, and confirm external redirection. Test whether the OAuth callback prefix can be extended to reach that endpoint. Deliver the crafted authorization URL to the victim, capture the fragment at the exploit server, and use the token against the API. Review redirect allowlists and token audience. The target phases are redirect discovery, callback chaining, token capture, API abuse, and policy review.

metadata.title: OAuth Access Token Theft via Open Redirect: Testing Methodology
associated_labs: OAuth Access Token Theft via Open Redirect

text: Testing playbook: enumerate client pages that call postMessage and inspect the target origin and the data sent. Test whether authentication-related pages can be framed, and whether their URL contains a token. Build an attacker page that frames the target and logs received messages. Review frame-ancestors and listener origin checks. The target phases are page enumeration, messaging analysis, framing, token capture, and policy review.

metadata.title: OAuth Access Token Theft via a Proxy Page: Testing Methodology
associated_labs: OAuth Access Token Theft via a Proxy Page

text: Testing playbook: capture the session token and decode its header and payload. Identify the claims that drive authorization, then modify sub or role without re-signing and replay the request. Confirm access to a privileged endpoint. Review server code and configuration for decode-only calls and disabled verification. The target phases are capture, claim identification, tampered replay, endpoint confirmation, and code review.

metadata.title: JWT Unverified Signature Bypass: Testing Methodology

text: Testing playbook: decode the header and note the algorithm and key hint. Re-sign or strip the signature while setting alg to none and its case variants, then replay with an escalated subject. Confirm access and review the verifier configuration for algorithm pinning. The target phases are header analysis, algorithm substitution, signature removal, claim escalation, and configuration review.

metadata.title: JWT alg=none Acceptance: Testing Methodology

text: Testing playbook: capture a token and identify HS256 versus an asymmetric algorithm. Run hashcat in JWT mode against common-secret and environment-specific wordlists. On recovery, sign a token with an escalated subject and replay it. Confirm access to a privileged endpoint. The target phases are capture, identification, cracking, forgery, and access confirmation.
